summary: Empirical delivery contract for the focused-keys transport. Every value below was measured against the deterministic testapp fixture; delivery is counted only when the app's own FIXTURE_KEY marker is observed through get_logs.

keyDownDwell.finding: A key-down/key-up pair posted with no dwell is never delivered. The simulator's event loop samples key state, so the pair must straddle at least one sample.
keyDownDwell.note: This is the defect that failed Task 15's original CGEvent gate: the transport posted key-up 7.4 microseconds after key-down.

firstKeyAfterAppLaunch.finding: The simulator consumes exactly the first key event delivered after an app launches. Reproduced 10/10 on fresh app launches.
independentOf: elapsed time since the app started (still dropped after 12s)
whether the press followed an activation transition
AXRaise, AXFocused, or AXMain on the simulator window

adopted.rationale: kVK_Shift. A modifier reaches the window server like any key and absorbs the consumed event, but Connect IQ can never decode it as a device button, so it is safe to send before every press without tracking which app launch was already warmed.
adopted.measurement: warm-up emitted no fixture marker; the following press delivered on both SDKs

activeApplicationObservation.finding: NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication and NSWorkspace.runningApplications are refreshed from main-run-loop notifications. An async MCP stdio server never pumps one, so both freeze at whatever was active when the process started.
activeApplicationObservation.evidence: A live gate recorded 154 consecutive identical polls naming the launching terminal while a freshly spawned process confirmed the Simulator was frontmost the whole time. This produced the 2026-08-02 simulator_focus_failed blocker; the activation itself had succeeded.

alternativesMeasured.CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo front normal-: live, but reports the front window owner, which is wrong when the active application has no windows
alternativesMeasured.NSRunningApplication(processIdentifier:): live and correct when the instance is constructed fresh on every call

activeApplicationObservation.adopted: NSRunningApplication(processIdentifier:).isActive, constructed per call, is the authorization for posting. Keys posted to the session tap are delivered to the active application, so this is the exact precondition.

activation.note: NSWorkspace.openApplication also activates (52-253ms measured) but re-opens the bundle through Launch Services. Both were measured; the accessibility attribute is used because it activates in place and needs only the Accessibility grant this server already holds.

menu.finding: Never delivered on fenix6xpro at any dwell (0/8 across both SDKs at 50ms, 400ms and 1200ms).
menu.reason: fenix 6X has no menu key. Menu is a long press of up; callers use press_button with button=up and holdMs>=1000.
menu.removedFrom: the profile button order and both SDK entries

keypadEnter.finding: no device button; produced no marker

backgroundDelivery.finding: CGEvent.postToPid delivers nothing to the simulator even with a correct dwell (0/4 buttons, app backgrounded).
backgroundDelivery.note: Re-verified deliberately, because Task 15 rejected this route while the zero-dwell defect was present. The rejection stands for the correct reason.

acceptance.surface: installed signed server at ~/.simulator-mcp/bin/simulator-mcp driven over real MCP stdio
acceptance.sequence: initialize -> tools/list -> list_devices -> sim_start -> run_app -> press_button -> get_logs
cases: enter after backgrounding to a windowless app
acceptance.result: 2 runs per SDK, 6/6 delivered in each; 24/24 presses total
acceptance.negative: allowFocus=false while backgrounded returns focus_required and posts no event
acceptance.markerAuthority: app-owned FIXTURE_KEY/FIXTURE_PAGE/FIXTURE_SELECTED/FIXTURE_BACK lines read through get_logs; a successful tool result is never treated as delivery evidence
